chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Discipline the orphan with what you discipline your child with, and strike him with what you strike your child with.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: How should an orphan be disciplined according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration from Imam Ali (AS) via the chain of Ghayath ibn Ibrahim underscores the principle of equity in child-rearing, extending paternal authority and affection to orphans as if they were one's own offspring. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating orphans into the family structure with identical disciplinary standards, preventing both neglect and excessive harshness. This guidance serves as a practical model for social justice within the domestic sphere, reinforcing the spiritual merit of treating the vulnerable with familial intimacy.
